description: 1. The agent must locate the SKILL.md / pharmgx_reporter.py tool and understand its CLI interface. 2. The agent must identify the correct raw genetic data file (`lab_results/genomics/raw/sample_GX_PT2024_042.txt`) amid ~13 distractor files — it is in 23andMe format with a comment-header block. 3. The agent must invoke `python pharmgx_reporter.py --input lab_results/genomics/raw/sample_GX_PT2024_042.txt --output pharmgx_report` — crucially, the `--output` flag takes a BASENAME (not a full path with extension), and the tool auto-appends `.md`. 4. The tool parses the 23andMe format, extracts 31 pharmacogenomic SNPs across 12 genes, calls star alleles, determines metabolizer phenotypes, and looks up CPIC drug recommendations for 51 medications. 5. The final artifact `pharmgx_report.md` must contain: markdown headers, gene names (CYP2C19, CYP2D6, etc.), star allele notation (*1, *2, etc.), metabolizer phenotype descriptions, and drug recommendation tables. An agent relying on generic training data will fail because: (a) it won't know about the specific `pharmgx_reporter.py` CLI and its `--output basename` convention, (b) it may produce its own report rather than running the proprietary tool, and (c) it may not know which file among the distractors is the valid 23andMe-formatted input.
